haiku-low.q1: Captured amount minus pending and succeeded refunds on that payment. Failed refunds are not subtracted.
haiku-low.q2: Retry up to 3 times with the same idempotency key. If all attempts fail, the record stays pending, not failed, because the provider may have made the refund. Step 7 resolves it.
haiku-low.q3: No retry. The refund is marked failed with the provider's message, saved in step 9. A failed refund never retries; a new submission creates a new refund.
haiku-low.q4: The refund's status becoming succeeded, saved by step 9. This happens via a refund.succeeded webhook or the hourly reconciliation job. The email follows the commit.
haiku-low.q5: Succeeded refunds only: below captured amount gives Partially refunded, equal gives Refunded. It recalculates in step 9's transaction when a refund's status is saved.
haiku-low.q6: The payment row lock. The refund check and pending-record insert happen under it in one transaction, so a second request waits until the first ends, then sees its result.
haiku-low.q7: The server generates a random UUID when it inserts the refund record in step 3. It is stored on the record and reused for every retry.
haiku-low.q8: Bad signatures are rejected. Events are matched by provider refund id. Only pending records move to final under the payment lock; duplicates change nothing, conflicts are audited, and the email flag prevents resending.
haiku-low.q9: Pending, not failed, because the provider may already have made the refund. Step 7 later checks or re-sends with the same key to resolve it.
haiku-low.q10: The hourly reconciliation job. With a provider id it checks status: pending changes nothing, final goes to step 9. Without an id, under 24 hours it re-sends the same key; 24 hours or older it stays pending and is audited once.
haiku-low.q11: The page waits until step 4 ends, then shows the record status: pending with a note that the provider has not confirmed, or failed with the provider message. It does not update until reload.

sonnet.q1: The refundable amount: captured amount minus the sum of pending and succeeded refunds on that payment (failed refunds are not subtracted).
sonnet.q2: The server retries up to 3 times with the same idempotency key. An accepted retry is handled like a normal acceptance, and a 4xx on a retry goes to step 5. If every attempt times out or gets a 5xx, the record stays pending and is resolved later by the reconciliation job (step 7).
sonnet.q3: No retry. The server passes status failed and the provider's message to step 9, which saves them (audit actor is the admin, or system for a re-send from the job). A failed refund no longer counts toward the refundable amount and is never retried. A new submission makes a new refund with a new record and key.
sonnet.q4: Step 9 committing a change to succeeded, whether triggered by a webhook or the reconciliation job. The email is sent right after the commit. The hourly email pass retries succeeded refunds whose email-sent flag is unset.
sonnet.q5: It is recalculated from succeeded refunds only, in step 9, when a refund status changes to succeeded or failed. No succeeded refunds gives normal. A succeeded total below the captured amount gives Partially refunded. A succeeded total equal to the captured amount gives Refunded. Pending and failed refunds are ignored, so a pending refund does not change it.
sonnet.q6: In step 3, in one database transaction, the server takes the payment row lock. A second request for the same payment waits until the first ends, then sees its result. The refundable amount (which counts pending refunds) is computed under the lock, and a request over it is rejected. The provider call is made outside the lock, but pending refunds already count.
sonnet.q7: It is a random UUID the server generates when it inserts the refund record in step 3. It is stored on the refund record and reused for every retry, including re-sends by the reconciliation job.
sonnet.q8: A record moves only from pending to a final status. Step 9 takes the payment row lock and saves the status only if the record is still pending. If it is already final with the same status, nothing changes and nothing is audited. If it is final with a different status, nothing changes and the conflict is audited. The email is triggered only by a committed change to succeeded, and the email-sent flag on the refund record means it is never emailed again once set. Webhooks with an unknown provider refund id return an error so the provider resends.
sonnet.q9: It stays pending, not failed, because the provider may already have made the refund. Step 7 (the reconciliation job) resolves it.
sonnet.q10: The reconciliation job (step 7), hourly. Pending with a provider id: it asks the provider for the status. If still pending, nothing changes. If succeeded or failed, it passes the status to step 9 directly, using step 6 rules. Pending with no id and under 24 hours old (from creation): it re-sends create-refund with the same key and saves the id. If the reply shows a final status, it applies it. A 4xx goes to step 5 with system as actor. Pending with no id and 24 hours or older: no re-send, stays pending, one audit entry written the first time, and a person must check. If the provider is unreachable, the record stays pending until the next run.
sonnet.q11: The page waits until step 4 ends (accepted, rejected or retries used up, up to about 40 seconds). The server then returns the status from our refund record. If accepted or retries used up, the page shows pending with a note that the provider has not confirmed the refund and the status will update by itself (not an error). If rejected, it shows failed with the provider's message once step 9 has saved it, otherwise the pending note. Later changes appear only after a reload.
